# PowerPoint Builder for DeepSeek Harness

A plugin bundle that lets an agent build real Microsoft PowerPoint decks: pastel
palettes, ten reusa

ble slide templates with exact geometric centering, styled
text boxes, internet images, charts rende

red by Python, highlighted code cards,
and LaTeX formulas — matrices, integrals, sums with limits —

typeset by the
plugin itself, with no LaTeX installation. It also ships a **Presentations**
agent mo
de tuned for deck work.

The `.pptx` package (ZIP + OOXML) is written by the plugin itself, so there is
no Office dependency,

no network round-trip after an image is embedded, and the
file stays valid after every call.

Or use **Plugins → Install** in the Harness UI and paste the package name.
After a restart the tools

show up in every mode, and a new **Presentations**
agent preset appears in the mode picker for a ne

n every mode, and a new **Presentations**
agent preset appears in the mode picker for a new session.
From a local checkout, pass the absolute directory instead of the package name.
## Presentations mode

The preset adds a persona that knows the workflow — inspect before editing,
build from templates, ci

te data sources, typeset mathematics with
`pptx_add_math`, finish with `present` — plus a focused to

olset: the `pptx_*`
tools, file reading, web search/fetch, `present`, `todo_write`,
`ask_user_questi

on`, and compaction. The tools themselves are registered
host-wide, so they are also usable outside

ompaction. The tools themselves are registered
host-wide, so they are also usable outside this mode.
## Tools
| Tool | What it does |
| `pptx_create` | Creates a deck on a pastel palette: size (`16:9` / `4:3`), palette, default font,

accent, page-number placement. |
| `pptx_gallery` | Builds a ready-made reference deck: `features` t
ours every template, alignment, list style and chart kind; `showcase` is a polished business deck. |
| `pptx_add_slide` | Adds a slide from a template (`title`, `section`, `content`, `split-left`, `sp

lit-right`, `chart`, `code`, `closing`, `blank`) with a heading, text, presenter and photo. |
| `ppt
x_add_text` | Arbitrary text box: `role`, `x`/`y`/`w`/`h`, `font_size`/`font_face`/`bold`/`italic`/`

underline`/`color`/`align`/`valign`/`bullet`. |
| `pptx_add_image` | Downloads an image by `url` (or

reads a local `path`), embeds the bytes and places it; the aspect ratio is preserved. |
| `pptx_add
_chart` | Renders a chart from data (bar, stacked bar, line, area, pie, donut) with Python and embed

s it. |
| `pptx_add_code` | Renders a code snippet as a dark card with syntax highlighting, line num

bers, a file-name header and highlighted lines. |
| `pptx_add_math` | Typesets a LaTeX formula — mat
rices, integrals, sums with limits, fractions, Greek letters — and embeds it as a crisp transparent

picture. |
| `pptx_update_element` | Moves, resizes, restyles, retypes or replaces an existing eleme

nt by id. |
| `pptx_remove` | Deletes one element by id, or a whole slide by its 1-based number. |
|
`pptx_inspect` | Lists the template, palette and every element with ids, geometry in inches, text,
fonts and sources. |

Coordinates are inches from the top-left corner of the slide (16:9 is
13.333 × 7.5), font sizes are

points, colours are `#RRGGBB`, a basic colour
name, or a palette keyword (`ink`, `muted`, `accent`,

s are `#RRGGBB`, a basic colour
name, or a palette keyword (`ink`, `muted`, `accent`, `background`).
## Templates
| Template | Layout |
| `title` | Oversized centred heading, subtitle below, presenter line in the bottom-right corner. Pa

ge number off. |
| `section` | Divider: heading and subtitle centred on the slide. |
| `content` | C

entred heading on top, a fixed-width text column underneath. |
| `split-right` | Photo fitted and ce

ntred in the right half; heading and text centred in the left half. |
| `split-left` | Mirrored: pho

to on the left, text on the right. |
| `chart` | Heading and caption on top, the lower two thirds re

served for `pptx_add_chart`. |
| `code` | Heading and subtitle on top, the rest reserved for `pptx_a

dd_code`. |
| `math` | Heading and subtitle on top, an optional statement under them, the rest reser

ved for `pptx_add_math`. |
| `closing` | Large centred "Спасибо за внимание" (override with `title`)

, optional subtitle. |
| `blank` | Nothing but the background. |

Every template centres its content inside its own region: the photo in its half,
the heading and tex
t in theirs, blocks centered vertically.
## Palettes

`pptx_create` takes `palette`: `sand` (default), `mint`, `lavender`, `sky`,
`rose`. A palette define

s the pastel background of every slide, the body ink,
the muted secondary colour, the accent, and th
e chart series colours.
## Alignment and lists
Alignment and text shape are parameters, not template defaults:
| Parameter | Values |

| `align` | `left`, `center`, `right`, `justify` for the `text` block |
| `title_align` | the same f

or the heading and subtitle |
| `bullet` | `true` for a bulleted list, `false` (default) for one sol

ding and subtitle |
| `bullet` | `true` for a bulleted list, `false` (default) for one solid block |

Defaults: `content` is left-aligned, `split-left` / `split-right` are centred
[该节后续省略]
## Requirements

- Charts and code cards are rendered by Python with Pillow. Harness ships such
a runtime, and the pl

ugin finds it automatically; on another setup point
`pythonPath` at an interpreter where `import PIL

` works.
- Images must be direct PNG, JPEG, GIF or BMP links. WebP and SVG are rejected
with an acti
onable message, because PowerPoint cannot render them.
## Limitations

- Charts cover bar, stacked bar, line, area, pie and donut. No maps, heatmaps or
3D charts.
- Formul

as are high-resolution pictures, not editable PowerPoint equations: to
change one, remove the elemen

t and add it again. The typesetter covers the
subset above, not the whole LaTeX language — no equati

on numbering, `\tikz`,
chemistry packages or custom macros.
- Photo templates fit the whole image (c

ontain); there is no cropping.
- Animations, speaker notes, tables and native PowerPoint charts are

not
created.
- An image is downloaded when the tool runs; after that the deck is
self-contained.
